description: I'm Marco, a GIS student at Western building 3D maps of wildfire, hazards and satellites. My plan: Harmonization of MODIS and VIIRS Hot Spots. NASA's fire record is passing from aging MODIS to newer VIIRS sensors, and joined wrong it fakes a jump in fire. I'll fix that, build a BC fire calendar from 2000 to today, and open with a live 3D satellite globe. Just me so far. Into stats, web dev, video or storytelling? Reach out. Iron sharpens iron. Fully virtual.
summary: NASA has watched the planet burn for 25 years, but the record is split in two. MODIS (2000 on) uses 1 km pixels. VIIRS (2012 on) uses 375 m pixels and logs about 5x more hotspots for the same fires, so a stitched record shows a fake jump in 2012. Burn Calendar fixes that. We rasterize every FIRMS hotspot from 197 countries and territories onto a common 5 km grid, learn a MODIS-to-VIIRS conversion for each country from the overlap years, and test it by hiding one year at a time and predicting it (3.9% average error). The result is a 4D globe of 11,908 hexagon columns from 2000 to 2025, plus a LIVE layer of the last 7 days. Click anywhere to get a month-by-year burning calendar, this week and this month vs their historical medians, and a CSV download. Along the way we found that Terra and Aqua have drifted about an hour off their original overpass times since 2022, a trap a naive calibration falls straight into. As an independent check, carbon monoxide from MOPITT, the Canadian Space Agency instrument on Terra, spikes where and when our record says fires were unusual.
details:
What it does

Burn Calendar turns NASA's two fire satellite records into one consistent 25-year record (Nov 2000 to Dec 2025) and shows it on an interactive 3D globe. MODIS (2000 on) uses 1 km pixels; VIIRS (2012 on) uses 375 m pixels and logs about 5x more hotspots for the same fires, so a stitched record shows a fake jump in 2012. We remove that jump.

- World globe: 11,908 H3 hexagons (~12,000 km² each) as 3D columns sized by burning activity. Press play to run 2000 to 2025 month by month.

- Modes: HARMONIZED, RAW STITCHED (shows the fake 2012 jump: world total x3.94 from 2011 to 2012; harmonized x1.00, matching MODIS-only x1.02), LIVE (last 7 days from FIRMS near-real-time vs the same time of year over 25 years), and SMOKE · CSA (carbon monoxide from the Canadian MOPITT instrument).

- Area of interest: click the globe or type lat/lon + radius. You get a month x year burning calendar (inferno colour ramp, colour-blind safe), the fire season profile, yearly totals, top months on record, and this week and this month vs their historical median (anomaly %).

- Downloads: monthly CSV (harmonized, raw, median, anomaly) and the calendar as PNG.

- BC deep dive: live satellite orbits (SGP4) showing when each fire satellite next passes over BC, a daily calendar, a hotspot map and the full calibration.

How it works (GIS method)

1. Vector to raster: both sensors' hotspot points are rasterized onto one 0.05° grid as burning cell-days, which removes most of the pixel-size difference (BC raw ratio 4.58x falls to 1.94x).

2. Overlay and joins on a common key (cell ID, date): in Canada, a left join shows VIIRS confirms 77.6% of MODIS detections. A right join shows MODIS sees only 40% of what VIIRS sees, which is the small-fire gap the model bridges.

3. Attribute join: each hexagon carries its country ID; a per-country fit VIIRS = e^a × MODIS^b (log space, volume-weighted) is joined on it. 147 countries get their own fit; small ones use the pooled global fit.

4. Orbit drift trap: from FIRMS acquisition times, Aqua drifted from 12:48 to 13:53 local solar time and Terra from 11:28 to 10:21 (2012 to 2025). We calibrate only on 2012 to 2022, when the orbits still matched the 2000 to 2011 era.

5. Validation:

- Hiding one year at a time and predicting it: world 3.9% error (volume-weighted), BC 8.1%. The top 15 fire countries are all under 7%.

- Blind test (fit on 2012 to 2022, predict 2023 to 2025): world -2.5% / +5.2% / -4.9%.

- Pipeline check: our counts match an independent recount of the raw FIRMS rows exactly.

6. Smoke check with Canadian Space Agency data: MOPITT carbon monoxide 2000 to 2024 (2,077 daily files, ~87 GB streamed). We handled its own version-change trap by subtracting the world-average CO change each month. Fire-season correlation of fire vs smoke anomalies: Siberia 0.49, BC 0.44, SE Australia 0.42. The biggest CO spikes match BC 2023, California Sep 2020 and Black Summer Dec 2019.

7. Data-type traps handled:

- MODIS confidence is a 0 to 100 number; VIIRS uses l/n/h text.

- The acquisition time is stored as text with a leading zero.

- Only vegetation fires are kept (no gas flares or volcanoes).

Benefits and intended impact

Fire managers, emergency planners and scientists can ask "is this fire season unusual for this place?" for anywhere on Earth and get an answer that doesn't depend on which satellite was flying. Live: right now California is +150% above normal for this time of year. Long-term trend studies stop being fooled by the 2012 sensor switch and the satellites' drift.

What makes it creative

- It treats the satellites themselves as a source of error: we measured their orbit drift from the data.

- A second, independent instrument (Canada's MOPITT) checks whether smokeays fires were unusual.

- 25 years of the planet burning, playable as a 4D globe.

Factors we considered

- Pixel size vs counting method.

- Satellite overpass times and orbit drift.

- Honest validation on years the model never saw.

- A colour-blind-safe ramp.

- Processing-version changes in the CO data.

- Keeping it a static web page anyone can open without a login.

Tools

Python (csv, h3), JavaScript, Three.js, satellite.js (SGP4), HTML canvas, Netlify hosting, FFmpeg for the video.
